{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE - Turns pictures into the model's own format and back. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can hand back a transparent picture.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - Character - The character you want on the sheet. In the prompt it is <image1>. A full-body picture works best. A head-and-shoulders portrait works too: the model draws the rest of the body, in clothes that match.
  • 2. Pick Orientation and Size - The size of the sheet. It opens on 1920 x 1088, a wide 16:9 sheet. The 3:2 sizes are a little narrower and draw the figures a little bigger. The starred sizes are Qwen's native 2K ones and much slower. Your picture goes to the model whole whatever you pick.
  • 3. Character Sheet Prompt - The prompt, in four boxes you can edit one at a time: Character sheet (what to draw and how it stands), Views (how many, and which, from left to right), Keep the same (what has to match your picture) and Background. They are joined line by line into one prompt, and an empty box is skipped. Right-click the node for its settings, where you can rename a box or change how they are joined.
  • 4. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same sheet, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your picture and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Math Expression - Works out how many megapixels the size from step 2 has, so your picture is read at the same number of pixels as the sheet.
  • Scale Image to Total Pixels - Works out the size your picture is read at: that many pixels, in steps of 32, in your picture's own shape. Only that size is used.
  • Get Image Size - Reads that size as a width and a height for Resize Crop Pixaroma under it.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma - Scales your picture to that size and trims the few pixels that do not fit, so the model gets the whole picture and nothing is stretched.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads the prompt from step 3 and your picture. Its resolution is set to 0, which takes the picture as it comes from the helpers. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • Empty Latent Image - The blank canvas for the result, at the size from step 2. The encoder's own canvas would always copy picture 1's shape.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from ComfyUI's own template.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the sheet and saves it to your output folder as a PNG. There is no Compare here: the sheet is a new picture in a new shape, so there is nothing to line up with your picture.

The dark Run Timer above it shows how long the last Run took.

{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

One picture of a character in, a wide character sheet out: the same character three times in a row, seen from the front, from the side and from the back, in the same style as your picture, on a plain white background. Photos, 3D cartoons, anime and flat drawings each keep their own look.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How long a Run takes

SizePixelsNew picture, prompt or sizeNew seed only
1248 x 832about 1 MP, 3:28 s6 s
1376 x 768about 1 MP, 16:98 s7 s
1728 x 1152about 2 MP, 3:218 s14 s
1920 x 1088about 2 MP, 16:9, the default18 s15 s
2560 x 1440about 3.7 MP, 16:939 s32 s
2528 x 1696native 2K, 3:249 s40 s
2752 x 1536native 2K, 16:948 s39 s

Change the picture, the prompt or the size and the model reads your picture again, which is the first time column. Change only the seed and it reuses what it read, which is the second.

Native 2K at 16:9 took about three times as long as the default 1920 x 1088. The 1 MP sizes still draw a clean sheet; try your prompt there and go up once you like it.

 Editing the prompt

Each box is one part of the prompt, so change only the box you need and the others keep working. <image1> is your picture.

  • Background - Change the colour word: Plain solid light gray background. Light gray, black and pastel blue were all tested (6 sheets): three views every time, and on black the character stays brightly lit, because the lighting line is in the first box.
  • Views - Always say how many. When this box listed the three views without the number, 8 of 16 sheets came out with an extra figure, usually a second back view. With the number, every sheet in the tests below had exactly the views asked for. For four views, write Four views side by side in one row, all at the same size, from left to right: front view facing the viewer, three-quarter view, side view in profile facing right, back view seen from behind. and keep a 16:9 size: 4 of 4 came out right.
  • Keep the same - Add anything the model forgets, like a bag, a logo or which hand holds something.
  • Character sheet - How the character stands. For a sheet you want to model in 3D, change standing in a relaxed neutral pose to standing in an A-pose with the arms held slightly away from the body. It is a request, not a guarantee: in 4 tests the arms came clearly away from the body on 2, and only a little on the others.

 Picking the size

Both shapes held the three views: 16:9 in all 32 tests and 3:2 in all 8, where the figures come out a little bigger. The picture goes to the model whole at every size, so there is nothing to trim or line up.

Tested with this prompt on 9 characters: four photos of people (two of them head-and-shoulders portraits), the 3D cartoon bunny, an anime girl, a flat vector robot, a painted elf and a cat. Every sheet showed front, side facing right and back, in that order, in the style of the picture. The cat stays sitting, since that is how it sits in its photo.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at 1920 x 1088, it took 15 s, against 21 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out the same, with small differences in the fine details. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder. Measured on a 1920 x 1088 sheet: 21 s with the models unloaded first, 15 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 21 GB during these runs, at 2528 x 1696. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 The memory node (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache)

While it renders, the model keeps what it has worked out about your picture and the prompt in a cache, so it does not redo that on every step. The teal node says where that cache lives. Leave it on auto / default: auto keeps the cache in spare graphics memory and moves it to system RAM when that runs out.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 810, "height": 1595, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}
